theory.intro: A **precedence table** lists each activity, its duration, and its **immediate predecessors** — the activities that must finish directly before it starts. Drawing the table as a network puts each activity on a directed edge between two vertices.
facts: Each activity is drawn as one directed edge, labelled with its name and its duration.
Every activity with no immediate predecessors is drawn from a single start vertex.
An activity begins at a vertex reached by every immediate predecessor, either directly or through a zero-duration dummy path.
Every activity with no successors is joined to a single finish vertex.
Do not draw a vertex until you are certain of every activity that starts there.
steps: Draw a start vertex and an edge for every activity with no immediate predecessors
Add each remaining activity as an edge beginning at a vertex reached by every immediate predecessor, directly or through a dummy path
Insert a dashed dummy activity where two activities share only part of their predecessor list
Join every activity with no successors to a single finish vertex

workedExamples.question_text:
Construct the network diagram for this project. Durations are in hours.

| Activity | Duration | Immediate predecessors |
|---|---:|---|
| A | 3 | — |
| B | 4 | — |
| C | 2 | A |
| D | 5 | B |
| E | 6 | C, D |
| F | 2 | E |

Construct a network diagram for the project, clearly identifying both dummy activities. Durations are in minutes.

| Activity | Duration | Immediate predecessors |
|---|---:|---|
| A | 7 | — |
| B | 4 | — |
| C | 6 | — |
| D | 8 | A, B |
| E | 9 | B, C |

workedExamples.solution_text:
$A$ and $B$ leave Start, so neither has an immediate predecessor.

$C$ starts where $A$ ends. $D$ starts where $B$ ends, but the dummy also brings the dependency on $A$ to that vertex. Therefore, $D$ needs both $A$ and $B$.

$E$ follows $C$, and $F$ follows $D$. Record the real activities only; the dummy passes a dependency and has no separate activity row.

| Activity | Duration (minutes) | Immediate predecessors |
|---|---:|---|
| A | 4 | — |
| B | 7 | — |
| C | 2 | A |
| D | 6 | A, B |
| E | 5 | C |
| F | 3 | D |

workedExamples.question_text:
Which network description matches this precedence table? Durations are in days. Every description uses these durations as edge labels and joins all final activities to one Finish vertex.

| Activity | Duration | Immediate predecessors |
|---|---:|---|
| A | 6 | — |
| B | 4 | — |
| C | 3 | A |
| D | 7 | A, B |
| E | 2 | C |

A. $A$ and $B$ leave Start. $C$ follows $A$ only. A dummy runs from the end of $A$ to the end of $B$, where $D$ starts. $E$ follows $C$.

B. $A$ and $B$ leave Start and end at one shared vertex, where both $C$ and $D$ start. $E$ follows $C$.

C. $A$ and $B$ leave Start. $C$ follows $A$ only. A dummy runs from the end of $B$ to the end of $A$, where $C$ starts. $D$ follows $B$ only. $E$ follows $C$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Check each activity's starting vertex against its predecessor list.

Description A makes $C$ depend on $A$ only and $D$ depend on both $A$ and $B$ through the dummy. It also places $E$ after $C$.

Description B incorrectly makes $C$ wait for $B$ as well as $A$.

Description C reverses the dummy: it adds $B$ as a predecessor of $C$ and leaves $D$ dependent on $B$ only.

Correct answer: A.

foundation.question_text:
The precedence table below shows the activities in a car service.
Durations are in minutes.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Activity} & \text{Duration} & \text{Immediate predecessors} \\ \hline A & 3 & - \\ B & 5 & A \\ C & 2 & A \\ D & 4 & B \\ E & 6 & C \\ F & 1 & D, E \end{array}$
Draw the network diagram for this project.

A school play is prepared using the activities below.
Durations are in days.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Activity} & \text{Duration} & \text{Immediate predecessors} \\ \hline A & 4 & - \\ B & 6 & - \\ C & 3 & A \\ D & 2 & B \\ E & 5 & C, D \\ F & 2 & E \end{array}$
Draw the network diagram for this project.

foundation.solution_text:
$A$ leaves the start vertex, so it has no immediate predecessors.
$B$ and $C$ both begin where $A$ ends.
$D$ begins where $C$ ends, and $E$ begins where $B$ ends.
$F$ begins where $D$ ends.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Activity} & \text{Duration} & \text{Immediate predecessors} \\ \hline A & 6 & - \\ B & 4 & A \\ C & 3 & A \\ D & 5 & C \\ E & 2 & B \\ F & 7 & D \end{array}$

development.solution_text:
$A$ and $B$ both leave the start vertex, so neither has an immediate predecessor.
The vertex where $C$ starts is reached by $A$ directly and by $B$ through the dummy, so $C$ has immediate predecessors $A$ and $B$.
$D$ starts where $B$ ends, and $E$ starts where $D$ ends.

mastery.question_text:
A bridge maintenance project has the activities below.
Durations are in weeks.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Activity} & \text{Duration} & \text{Immediate predecessors} \\ \hline A & 6 & - \\ B & 9 & - \\ C & 4 & A \\ D & 5 & A, B \\ E & 3 & C \\ F & 7 & D \\ G & 2 & D \\ H & 1 & E, F \end{array}$
Draw the network diagram for this project.

mastery.solution_text:
$A$ and $B$ both leave the start vertex.
The vertex where $C$ and $H$ start is reached by $A$ directly and by $B$ through the dummy, so both have immediate predecessors $A$ and $B$.
$D$ starts where $B$ ends alone.
$E$ starts where $C$ ends, and $F$ starts where $D$ ends.
$G$ starts at the vertex where $E$, $F$ and $H$ all end.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{Activity} & \text{Duration} & \text{Immediate predecessors} \\ \hline A & 5 & - \\ B & 8 & - \\ C & 6 & A, B \\ D & 3 & B \\ E & 4 & C \\ F & 7 & D \\ G & 2 & E, F, H \\ H & 9 & A, B \end{array}$
